Auth.explanation: AuthController only validates the payload then hands everything off to AuthService. For individual receivers and volunteers, a selfie photo must yield a face descriptor before the account is created. The user row and exactly one role profile are written in a single transaction, then a token pair is issued and the refresh token is stored hashed. Three entry points but a single exit. Password login compares bcrypt hashes; Google and Firebase authenticate id tokens with their providers and auto-create a receiver account on first sign-in. All branches end at issueTokens, where the new refresh token is stored hashed. Locked accounts are blocked AFTER identity resolution, not before. Refresh rotates the token pair atomically and the old refresh is revoked inside the same transaction, so a leaked refresh token works exactly once. Logout revokes every still-live token for the account, which is also what ban and password-reset trigger. JwtAuthGuard protects the logout route via JwtStrategy. Redis only stores the SHA-256 hash of the reset token under a TTL key, so even a Redis dump leak cannot reset anyone's password. Both 'email not found' and 'account locked' return the same generic success message, blocking account enumeration. On success the flow revokes every refresh token and deletes the Redis key, making the token single-use.

AuthController.description: REST entry points for registration and account-existence lookups. Delegates all work to AuthService.

methods.+register(dto: RegisterDto, selfie: File: Validates payload + selfie, then calls AuthService.register. Returns the issued access/refresh token pair on success.
methods.+checkEmail(email: string): Promise<Exis: Lightweight existence check used by the FE to disambiguate 'email already in use' before the user fills the whole form.
methods.+checkPhone(phone: string): Promise<Exis: Same as checkEmail but for phone numbers; rate-limited to prevent enumeration.
methods.+login(dto: LoginDto, req: Request): Pro: Accepts email + password, forwards the request metadata (device info, IP) to AuthService.login.
methods.+firebase(dto: FirebaseLoginDto, req: Re: Accepts a Firebase id token, delegates to AuthService.loginWithFirebase which verifies the token and provisions a receiver account on first sign-in.
methods.+refresh(refreshToken: string, req: Requ: Rotates the refresh token: revokes the presented one, issues a new pair, and updates the device metadata.
methods.+logout(user: User): Promise<void>: Revokes all live refresh tokens for the authenticated user.
methods.+forgotPassword(dto: ForgotPasswordDto):: Always returns a generic success message; behind the scenes sends the reset email if the email exists and is not banned.
methods.+resetPassword(dto: ResetPasswordDto): P: Verifies the token against Redis, updates the password with bcrypt, revokes every refresh token for that user.

AuthService.description: Owns the registration transaction: extract face descriptor, hash password, persist user + role profile, persist hashed refresh token, issue JWT pair.

methods.+register(dto: RegisterDto, selfie: File: Extracts face descriptor from selfie (mandatory for individual/volunteer roles), hashes the password with bcrypt (>=12 rounds), writes user + role profile in a single Prisma transaction, then issues tokens.
methods.+checkEmailExists(email: string): Promis: Counts rows by email; returns a boolean without leaking whether the account is active.
methods.+checkPhoneExists(phone: string): Promis: Counts rows by phone; same privacy-preserving shape as checkEmailExists.
methods.-issueTokens(user: User): Promise<AuthRe: Signs short-lived access JWT, generates refresh token, stores its SHA-256 hash in refresh_tokens, returns both to the caller.
methods.+login(dto: LoginDto, deviceInfo: string: Looks up user by email, bcrypt-compares the password, enforces status != banned, then issues tokens and records device info on the refresh row.
methods.+loginWithFirebase(idToken: string, role: Calls FirebaseAdminService.verifyIdToken; on first sign-in auto-creates a receiver profile, then issues tokens.
methods.+refresh(rawToken: string, deviceInfo: s: Hashes the incoming raw token, looks up refresh_tokens, deletes it, signs a new access JWT and persists a new hashed refresh token.
methods.+logout(userId: string): Promise<void>: Deletes all refresh_tokens rows for the user; subsequent refresh attempts will fail.
methods.+forgotPassword(dto: ForgotPasswordDto):: Looks up the user; if found and active, generates a reset token, stores its hash in Redis with TTL, and emails the raw token.
methods.+resetPassword(dto: ResetPasswordDto): P: Hashes the presented token, looks up Redis, sets a new bcrypt password, deletes every refresh_token for the user, and deletes the Redis key.
methods.-hashResetToken(token: string): string: SHA-256 helper used before every Redis write/read.
methods.-passwordResetKey(tokenHash: string): st: Builds the namespaced Redis key, e.g. auth:password-reset:{hash}.

FaceMatchService.description: Face descriptor extraction and comparison using a local face-recognition model. Descriptors are 128-d vectors used for both 1:1 (live vs enrolled) and 1:N matching.

methods.+getFaceDescriptor(photo: File): Promise: Extracts a 128-d descriptor from the input photo; throws if no face is detected.
methods.+compare(a: number[], b: number[]): Matc: Compares two descriptors and returns the match score plus a boolean accepted flag.

StorageService.description: Local-disk image storage with MIME + magic-byte validation. Production deployments swap this implementation for S3 / R2 / Cloudinary without touching callers.

methods.+saveImage(file: File, subdir: string):: Validates the file, picks a path under {uploadRoot}/{subdir}/, writes the buffer, returns the public URL.
methods.+imageExists(url: string): Promise<boole: Cheap existence probe used by cleanup jobs.
methods.-matchesMagicBytes(buffer: Buffer, mimet: Verifies the file signature matches the declared MIME type.

JwtService.description: Wrapper around the jsonwebtoken library: signing access tokens and verifying incoming tokens on protected routes.

methods.+sign(payload: JwtPayload, options: Sign: Signs a JWT with the configured secret and TTL.
methods.+verify(token: string, options: VerifyOp: Verifies a JWT signature and expiry; throws on invalid or expired tokens.

PrismaService.description: Prisma ORM client wrapper. Each field exposes a model delegate used by services to issue typed queries and mutations.

FirebaseAdminService.description: Firebase Admin SDK wrapper; used to verify Google / Apple id tokens before issuing a session.

methods.+verifyIdToken(idToken: string): Promise: Validates a Firebase id token and returns the decoded payload; throws on invalid / expired tokens.

JwtAuthGuard.description: NestJS guard that enforces a valid JWT on every incoming request via JwtStrategy.

methods.+canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): boo: Returns true if the request carries a valid Bearer token; otherwise throws 401.

JwtStrategy.description: passport-jwt strategy: extracts the Bearer token, verifies it, and loads the corresponding User into req.user.

methods.+validate(payload: JwtPayload): Promise<: Loads the User referenced by the JWT payload; throws if the user no longer exists or is banned.

ThrottlerGuard.description: Rate-limit guard backed by @nestjs/throttler; protects /auth/* and other sensitive routes from brute force.

methods.+canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext): boo: Allows up to N requests per minute per IP / user; throws 429 when the quota is exceeded.

Redis.description: ioredis client; a thin wrapper around the most common Redis commands.

methods.+setex(key: string, ttl: number, value:: Sets a key with a TTL in seconds.
methods.+get(key: string): Promise<string>: Reads a string value; returns null on miss.
methods.+del(key: string): Promise<number>: Deletes a key and returns the count removed.

MailService.description: Outbound mail sender, currently backed by SMTP but designed to swap providers.

methods.+sendPasswordResetEmail(email: string, n: Sends the password-reset link to the user.
